papers.title_en: SuperMimic: Scaling Humanoid Whole-Body Control with One Differentiable World Model
papers.authors: Qiayuan Liao, Yiyang Shao, Junfeng Long, Kevin Zakka, Roberto Horowitz, Pieter Abbeel, Koushil Sreenath
papers.evidence: 人形机器人运动模仿与全身跟踪策略学习
papers.tldr: 人形全身控制依赖大规模运动跟踪，但现有无模型强化学习扩展成本极高。SuperMimic用单个可微世界模型学习共享动力学，并与跟踪策略联合训练，通过短想象展开的反向传播提供解析梯度。单GPU 3小时即超过128GPU训练7天的基线回报，GPU小时降超1000倍，失败数从179降至25。该工作移除算力瓶颈，使运动跟踪缩放律研究更可行。
papers.abstract_en: Tracking large human-motion datasets has become the dominant route to general, expressive humanoid whole-body control, but scaling across many motions is expensive. Current pipelines use model-free reinforcement learning, either merging per-motion specialists through lossy distillation, or brute-forcing a single policy with cluster-scale compute. SuperMimic amortizes learning across all motions with one differentiable world model of their shared dynamics, fit from logged transitions of a standard rigid-body simulator. The world model and the tracking policy train together in one loop, and backpropagation-through-time over short imagined rollouts gives the policy analytic gradients. Fast imagined rollouts and analytic gradients make policy learning efficient. In 3 hours on a single GPU, SuperMimic surpasses the return of a state-of-the-art motion tracker baseline trained for 7 days on 128 GPUs. It reduces GPU-hours by more than $1000\times$ and fails on only 25 of 129,514 benchmark motions, versus 179 failures for the baseline. After 9.8 hours on two GPUs, SuperMimic achieves zero failures. From 1 to 264 hours of motion, the world model's prediction error stays stable, and GPU-hours to a target return grow slowly. Our policy transfers to a physical Unitree G1 across diverse and acrobatic motions. SuperMimic removes compute as the bottleneck to scaling humanoid whole-body control, making it practical to measure motion-tracking scaling laws.

papers.title_en: OmniInteract: Towards Unified Whole-Body Interaction Control for Dual Humanoids
papers.authors: Yinghao Li, Tianyu Zhang, Zhuohao Li, Yi-Lin Wei, Fa-Ting Hong, Qing Zhang, Wei-Shi Zheng
papers.evidence: 面向双人形机器人的统一全身交互控制，采用表面感知重定向与残差策略学习
papers.tldr: 双人形物理交互需协调全身运动与精确接触，但人机形态差异会破坏重定向后的接触接口，且联合学习技能与伙伴协调难以随交互多样性扩展。OmniInteract用表面接触感知重定向联合重定向双人形，并以可扩展流式交互策略在冻结运动先验上生成伙伴条件残差。实验显示其提升重定向保真与双人形协调，并在技能增多时更好保留交互性能。真实部署实现接触建立、稳定全身协调与扰动恢复。
papers.abstract_en: Physical interaction is a key capability for humanoid collaboration, requiring coordinated whole-body motion and precise contact. However, learning diverse dual-humanoid interactions faces two major challenges: (1) human-robot morphological differences disrupt contact interfaces and spatial relationships during retargeting, and (2) jointly learning motor skills and partner coordination makes it difficult to retain control fidelity as interaction diversity grows. In this paper, we propose OmniInteract to address these challenges through surface-aware modeling and scalable residual policy learning. First, we introduce Surface Contact-Aware Retargeting, which leverages dense human-robot surface correspondences to jointly retarget both humanoids, preserving explicit interaction contact interfaces and their near-field geometric context. Second, we propose a Scalable Flow-based Interaction Policy for partner-conditioned residual generation. It factorizes dual-humanoid control into a reusable motor foundation and interaction-specific adaptations: partner-aware experts learn corrections over a frozen whole-body motion prior, while conditional flow matching unifies them in a shared residual action space. This enables scalable skill consolidation while retaining pretrained motor capabilities. Extensive experiments demonstrate that OmniInteract improves retargeting fidelity and dual-humanoid coordination while better retaining interaction performance as skill diversity grows. Real-world deployment further demonstrates successful contact establishment, stable whole-body coordination, and recovery from external perturbations.

papers.title_en: XoNav: An Exoskeleton as a Personalized Haptic Interface for Assisted Navigation
papers.authors: Debadrata Sarkar, Soumen Sen, Aman Arora
papers.evidence: 髋关节外骨骼结合IMU与LSTM步态状态估计输出步态同步提示
papers.tldr: 无视觉步行需要及时、无歧义的引导，但音频或振动提示常要求用户自行将信号转译为动作。XoNav 用四执行器髋部外骨骼在髋关节直接呈现前进、两级制动和两级转向触觉线索，并以双侧 LSTM 步态分类器协调提示时机。盲行导航中，参与者 98.8% 的行走距离保持在 0.75 m 宽通道内，平均行进速度每轮提升 4.9%。研究还验证了自主导航与未知障碍绕行可行性，表明髋部外骨骼可作为个性化触觉导航接口。
papers.abstract_en: Walking without vision requires timely, unambiguous guidance, yet many wearable aids encode directions as audio or vibrotactile signals that users must translate into movement. We present XoNav, a four-actuator hip exoskeleton that renders guidance cues directly at the hip joints. It renders an Advance cue and two-level Braking cues through sagittal-plane actuators and two-level Steering cues through frontal-plane actuators. A bilateral LSTM-based gait-state classifier uses two thigh-mounted IMUs to identify gait states, enabling haptic cues to be delivered in coordination with the wearer's gait while suppressing them during standing. The classifier generalized to unseen users with recalls of 95.2-97.9%, with mean detection delays of 38.6 and 63.1 ms for stance-to-swing and swing-to-stance transitions, respectively. Constrained human-in-the-loop Bayesian optimization personalized Braking for minimum resistance and Steering for maximum comfort while ensuring detectability and safety. All participants reliably distinguished between grades of their personalized cues and the firmest Braking cue remained below 53% of the safety limit. In blindfolded Wizard-of-Oz navigation trials along three paths, the participants kept 98.8% of the walked distance within a 0.75 m wide passage, with a 4.9% increase in mean progression speed per trial. A body-worn camera, RTAB-Map and Nav2 further enabled a feasibility study of autonomous navigation and detours around previously unmapped obstacles.

papers.title_en: Robust Real-Time Monocular Human Pose Estimation with Insole-Based Sensor Fusion
papers.authors: Liang Yu, Tao Zhu, Xiangqing Lu, Wenjian Luo, Liming Chen
papers.evidence: 融合鞋垫传感与单目视觉的下肢姿态与足地接触估计
papers.tldr: 单目实时人体姿态估计在遮挡或短时出框时，仅靠视觉难以重建可信的下肢运动与足地接触。为此，作者采集同步多模态数据，提出部位解耦时序融合框架，将鞋垫压力与加速度特征注入下肢分支，并用轻量协调器维持全身一致。在2D关键点、3D landmarks和SMPL三类实时骨干上，融合持续提升姿态精度、平滑性与步态指标，遮挡和视觉丢失下增益最显著。结果表明无侵入足部传感能补充物理可观测性，增强视觉受限场景的鲁棒性。
papers.abstract_en: Real-time monocular human pose estimation is an important sensing component for human-centered intelligent systems. While recent camera-based methods have achieved impressive accuracy, fundamental challenges persist, particularly when visual observations are incomplete, such as during lower-body occlusion or short out-of-frame intervals. In these challenging but common scenarios, vision-only systems often struggle to reconstruct physically plausible lower-limb motion and reliable foot-ground contact. Due to the highly unobtrusive and wearable nature of smart insoles, this paper investigates whether simple plantar pressure and acceleration sensors can effectively resolve these visually induced limitations. To systematically investigate this, we first collect a synchronized multimodal dataset and then propose a part-decoupled temporal fusion framework. The proposed model fuses foot-sensing features into the lower-body branch to compensate for incomplete visual evidence, while a lightweight coordinator exchanges information between the upper- and lower-body temporal representations to maintain whole-body consistency. The framework is evaluated with three representative real-time visual backbones based on 2D keypoints, 3D landmarks, and SMPL-based human mesh recovery. We evaluate our framework on three representative real-time visual backbones. Quantitative experiments demonstrate that incorporating simple foot sensors consistently improves pose accuracy, motion smoothness, and gait-related measurements over vision-only baselines, with the most significant gains observed under occlusion and short visual-dropout conditions. Ultimately, our results demonstrate that unobtrusive foot sensing provides vital and complementary physical observability when camera observations are temporarily unavailable.

papers.title_en: Reinforcement Learning Based Multi-Terrain Adaptive Whole-Body Control for a Quadruped Manipulator
papers.authors: Yanzhou Jin, Fei Suo, Chang Liu, Yasuhisa Hasegawa, Liming Chen, Yusuke Iwasawa, Yutaka Matsuo, Yaonan Zhu
papers.evidence: 面向复杂地形的腿足机器人强化学习全身控制
papers.tldr: 针对小型四足机械臂在复杂地形上运动与操作强耦合、末端行为易受地形扰动影响的问题，提出基于强化学习的全身控制框架。方法将混合任务表示与任务优先级全身学习结合，协调移动与操作并保持任务一致的末端执行器行为，同时搭建轻量四足机械臂平台。真实实验在30度斜坡、楼梯和可变形地形上成功部署。结果表明学习式全身控制可用于真实环境的地形自适应移动作业，并凸显任务一致协调的重要性。
papers.abstract_en: Legged robots equipped with manipulators offer promising capabilities for loco-manipulation tasks in unstructured environments. However, achieving task-consistent end-effector behavior during locomotion remains challenging due to terrain-induced disturbances and the strong coupling between locomotion and manipulation, particularly for small-scale quadruped platforms. A reinforcement-learning based whole-body control framework is proposed for quadruped loco-manipulation on complex terrain. The proposed framework combines a hybrid task representation with task-prioritized whole-body learning to coordinate locomotion and manipulation while preserving task-consistent end-effector behavior. A lightweight quadruped manipulator platform is further developed to validate the proposed framework on a small-scale quadruped system. Real-world experiments demonstrate successful deployment on complex terrains such as slopes up to 30 degrees, stairs, and deformable terrain. These results demonstrate the feasibility of deploying learned whole-body control policy for quadruped loco-manipulation in real-world environments and highlight the importance of task-consistent whole-body coordination for terrain-adaptive loco-manipulation.

papers.title_en: Action-Aligned Latent Planning for Versatile Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
papers.authors: Yutang Lin, Guanya Shi, C. Karen Liu
papers.evidence: 面向人形机器人全身移动操作的潜在规划
papers.tldr: 面向多样化人形移动操作，单一感知策略需统一高层决策并保留状态相关控制响应。FIBER 将冻结行为基础模型的可执行潜空间作为异构技能共享规划表示，用潜策略投影对齐任务策略与局部控制响应，并离线训练单一感知流规划器。还提出自适应时域 AH-BFM 支持精确控制与长时程全身行为。仿真三类任务平均成功率达42.0%，显著超过潜回放与运动学规划，并在 Unitree G1 上验证迁移、技能串联与条件引导。
papers.abstract_en: Learning a single perceptive policy for diverse humanoid loco-manipulation requires unifying high-level task decisions without losing the state-dependent physical responses that make each interaction succeed. This makes the representation between high-level planning and whole-body control critical: kinematic or contact targets provide compact abstractions but do not directly encode interaction-specific control responses, while directly predicting low-level actions requires the planner to model high-frequency closed-loop feedback. We propose FIBER, a framework that uses the executable latent space of a frozen behavioral foundation model (BFM) as a shared planning representation for heterogeneous interaction skills. Our latent policy projection (LPP) maps independently acquired task-specific policies into this representation by identifying latent commands whose induced actions match their local control responses, enabling lower-rate planning while retaining the BFM's high-frequency state feedback. After projection, we aggregate closed-loop latent rollouts from all skills and train a single perceptive flow planner entirely offline. We further introduce AH-BFM, an adaptive-horizon BFM trained with multi-gamma forward-backward (FB) learning to support both precise control and temporally extended whole-body behavior. We evaluate FIBER on box pickup, door opening, and object grasping in simulation and on a real Unitree G1 humanoid. Across 128 diverse variations per task in simulation, FIBER achieves 42.0% mean success, more than tripling projected latent replay (11.6%) and substantially outperforming kinematic planning (3.5%). Real-world experiments further demonstrate sim-to-real transfer, skill chaining, and conditional steering through the same unified planner.

papers.title_en: DiPLO: Self-distilled Diffusion Planning for Loco-manipulation
papers.authors: Shafeef Omar, Sebastian Sanokowski, Elham Daneshmand, Dian Yu, Daniel Cremers, Cordelia Schmid, Majid Khadiv
papers.evidence: 人体到人形重定向与强化学习全身跟踪
papers.tldr: DPO去除强任务条件依赖并用DA:PPO微调对齐执行能力。方法在取放搬运任务达99%成功率，较预训练45%显著提升，并可泛化未见目标。最终在Unitree G1实机重复执行且无需真实微调。
papers.abstract_en: Humanoid loco-manipulation is particularly challenging because it requires coordinating locomotion, balance, and object interaction, making it difficult to learn from limited demonstrations or from scratch through Reinforcement Learning (RL). We introduce DiPLO (self-distilled Diffusion Planning for Loco-manipulation), a framework that combines a self-distilled diffusion planner with a low-level whole-body tracking policy. Our planner is pretrained via supervised learning on motions derived from human-to-humanoid retargeting, while the tracker is trained via RL to execute them. DiPLO centers around two complementary post-training stages. First, we introduce Self-Distillation Diffusion Policy Optimisation (SD:DPO) to remove the planner's dependence on strong task conditioning, which we identify as a crucial ingredient for effective pretraining, as downstream fine-tuning does not recover comparable performance when it is omitted.. We then fine-tune this distilled model with Diffusion-Augmented Proximal Policy Optimization (DA:PPO), a maximum-entropy RL method for diffusion models, to improve task success and align generated plans with the frozen tracker's execution capabilities. Together, these stages enable motion generation through state-history and goal conditioning alone, enabling 99% task success in pick-carry-place tasks, compared to just 45% for the pretrained model. The resulting planner also generates motions for unseen object goals, with further evaluations on kicking and pushing/pulling tasks. Finally, we deploy our pipeline on the hardware, using our DA:PPO planner-tracker on a Unitree G1, achieving repeated successful executions without any real-world fine-tuning.

papers.title_en: Data-Efficient Learning from Demonstration for Humanoid Robots via Feature-Level Perception and Prompt-Based Object Detection
papers.authors: Keyhan Rayati, AliReza Beigy, Anoosheh Saadati, Pourya Shahverdi, Mehdi Tale Masouleh, Ahmad Kalhor, Wing-Yue Geoffrey Louie
papers.evidence: 提示式目标检测与深度感知用于人形机器人操作
papers.tldr: 视觉示教通常依赖大规模数据和端到端训练，难以用于人形机器人。本文提出数据高效LfD框架，以分层视觉预处理、Kinect人体关节估计、提示式目标检测和深度信息提取任务特征，并训练时序模型预测关节轨迹。在NAO上，拾放任务仅用16次示教达78%，100次达86%；推任务用8次示教达71%。该工作展示了少量示教下的人形机器人操作技能获取。
papers.abstract_en: Learning from Demonstration (LfD) allows robots to learn new skills from human examples; however, many vision-based methods require large datasets and resource-intensive end-to-end training. This paper introduces a data-efficient LfD framework for humanoid robots that learns manipulation skills from compact, task-specific features instead of raw images. The proposed approach integrates layered visual preprocessing, Kinect-based human joint estimation, prompt-based object detection, and depth information to extract human motion features and three-dimensional object locations from demonstration videos. These features are used to train a temporal deep learning model that predicts robot joint-angle trajectories for execution. The framework is implemented on a NAO humanoid robot, evaluated quantitatively in simulation, and demonstrated on physical hardware. In simulation, the robot achieves a 78% success rate on a pick-and-place task using only 16 demonstrations, which increases to 86% when trained with 100 demonstrations. The framework also achieves a 71% success rate on a pushing task using eight demonstrations, highlighting its effectiveness for data-efficient humanoid skill acquisition.

papers.title_en: Adaptive Traversal Tubes for Posture-Aware Navigation of Bipedal Humanoids
papers.evidence: 面向双足人形机器人的姿态感知导航与全身运动控制
papers.tldr: 双足人形机器人可通过调整身体偏航改变有效足迹，从而兼顾窄通道通行与社交避让，但现有导航缺乏姿态与速度的统一规划。本文提出姿态感知导航框架：以自适应通行管ATT表示沿参考路径的行为可行宽度场，融合几何间隙与社交舒适度；再用区间速度—航向IVH控制将宽度映射为连续正面—侧步姿态调度与全向速度命令。配套速度条件AMP策略，利用重定向正面/侧步动作与耦合速度跟踪奖励提升切换稳定性。当前预印本给出完整方法、仿真与实机演示，G1定量评估待后续。
papers.abstract_en: Bipedal humanoids can change their effective footprint by adjusting body yaw, enabling both narrow-passage traversal and socially aware yielding. This paper presents a posture-aware navigation framework centered on \emph{Adaptive Traversal Tubes} (ATT), \emph{Interval Velocity--Heading} (IVH) control, and a sidestep-enhanced AMP locomotion prior. ATT represents a behavior-feasible corridor width field along a reference path, unifying geometric clearance and social comfort into a continuous signal. IVH maps this width to a continuous frontal-to-sidestep posture schedule and omnidirectional velocity commands. A velocity-conditioned AMP policy, trained with GVHMR-retargeted frontal/sidestep motions and coupled \((v_x,v_y)\) tracking rewards, is designed to improve transition stability over a generic locomotion controller while remaining interchangeable with the default onboard policy. This preprint presents the full method; a planned evaluation protocol on a Unitree G1 is outlined, with quantitative results to follow. Demo videos of MuJoCo simulation and real-robot deployment are available at: github.com/lborogzj997/Humanoid-Navigation-in-Crowds-and-Narrow-Spaces.
